rated_messages.input_message: When you are stressed, it is easy to focus on the things that are going wrong. Take a few moments to focus on 5 things that have gone well or that you are thankful for this week.
If you find yourself with a few minutes to spare, it can be nice to read back over old messages. It's also a chance to reply to ones that you might have forgotten about!
If you miss doing something with your hands, try turning a coin or pen over and over with your fingers.
Take a minute to notice what the urge feels like in your body without smoking a cigarette. Notice what is going on. See what happens. Does the urge pass?
Try to stop smoking by setting yourself a rule. For example, "IF I am tempted, THEN I will chew on some mints" - make your own rule that will work for you.

Think about a happy memory to ease the difficulty of your urge. Is there something you have been wanting to do for a while that you know you would enjoy? Reading? Walking? Calling a friend? Doing a puzzle? Do something that matters to you instead of smoking.
Imagine this urge as just another backseat passenger that hopped in after seeing other people smoke. You are the driver and you still get to call the shots.
Feelings aren't permanent. They are always changing like the weather. Observe the storm that is coming, but don't fight it. Eventually the weather will change.
If you usually smoke while you talk on the phone, keep a pen and paper nearby to occupy your hands with doodling rather than smoking.
If you are tempted to smoke by being in this location, see if you can sit with that temptation for 1 minute. When the minute is over, do it again. Soon, it should pass.
